info_server: Enter the IP address or host name of your digitalSTROM server - only once: it applies to both interfaces the adapter uses.
help_host: IP address or hostname of the digitalSTROM server (port 8080 is used automatically)
label_validateCertificate: Validate TLS certificate of the DSS
help_validateCertificate: Only enable with a valid, non-self-signed certificate
info_token: The credentials (usually dssadmin - the same ones as for the dSS configurator) are used once to create the app token and are not stored. The instance has to be running for this.
help_appToken: Filled automatically when created - alternatively paste an existing app token here
help_dataPollInterval: Interval for polling meter data in seconds. Default 100s: a cycle reads two values per circuit, which keeps the adapter within the DSS rules 8/9 (at most one cyclic read per minute and circuit). Smaller values are allowed from 60s on but exceed that guideline. 0 disables polling.
help_deleteUnknownObjects: Warning: objects of temporarily unreachable devices are deleted too, including their history settings!
info_tls: A digitalSTROM server ships with a self-signed certificate, so the check is disabled by default. The connection is encrypted, but the adapter does not verify who it is talking to. Run the DSS and ioBroker in a trusted network segment, or use a host name with a valid certificate.
info_smartHome: Newer digitalSTROM servers offer a second, modern interface in addition - and that is what the second key here is for. The adapter uses it as a turbo for reading: **all meter values and all output values** (brightness, blind positions, colour values) arrive in one single request each instead of many individual ones. The startup finishes in seconds instead of minutes, values are fresh again quickly after scene calls, and your dSS is noticeably relieved. The key is created from the existing app token with one click - no password needed again - and works hand in hand with it. Should the Smart Home API ever not answer, the proven path takes over automatically.
label_useSmartHomeApi: Read meter and output values through the Smart Home API
help_useSmartHomeApi: Reads meter and output values bundled through the Smart Home API. Needs a dSS with firmware 1.19 or newer and the key below.
help_smartHomeApiKey: Created from the existing app token, no password needed. Visible in the dSS under System > Access Authorization.
info_token_role: The app token is the adapter's base access: **button presses, sensor values and all events arrive through it in real time**, and **every switching command** runs over it. Nothing works without it - create it once with your dSS credentials.
section_status: Division of labour between the two interfaces
info_status: The adapter joins both interfaces of your dSS into one team and uses the strongest one for each task: real-time events and control through the app token, bundled values through the Smart Home API. This page shows live which path is doing the work.
status_not_running: The instance is not running right now - the live status appears as soon as it does.
status_events_help: Button presses, sensor values, binary inputs and every switching command - in real time
status_meters_help: Power and energy of every circuit
status_outputs_help: Brightness, blind positions and colour values of the devices
token_created: App token created and placed into the field below - press Save to store it permanently.
key_created: API key created and taken over - press Save to store it permanently.
info_why: Your digitalSTROM server offers two interfaces with different strengths - and this adapter deliberately uses both. The app token delivers **events in real time** (button presses, sensor values, binary inputs) and executes **every switching command**. The Smart Home API bundles **all meter and output values into one single request each**. Together this means: the adapter starts in seconds instead of minutes, values are fresh again quickly after scene calls, and your dSS carries noticeably less load - at full reliability, because should the Smart Home API ever not answer, the proven path takes over automatically. The Status tab shows which path is doing the work right now.
status_connection_help: Classic interface is reachable and logged in
